role: Extension of TrendsV2View holding the metric chart card (chips picker, Swift Charts dots/band/rolling line/scrub marks), the 2x2 stats grid, the Insights bullets, and the pure static series builders (metric extraction, rolling mean, stats cells, variation/outlier stats, direction sentences).
types: TrendsV2View: extension — chart, stats grid, insights
TrendsV2View.MetricPoint: struct (Identifiable, id = date) — one (date,value) sample
TrendsV2View.GridCell: struct — one stats-grid cell (label, value, subline, formatted delta, numeric deltaPercent, higherIsBetter)
toplevel: Only type declarations (MetricPoint, GridCell) inside the extension; no stored state, no globals.

flags.text: Two deltaColor functions colour the same 'vs baseline' delta with different palettes: the scrub pill uses AppTheme.wongOptimalText/wongCautionText (contrast-adjusted text variants) while the stats grid uses AppTheme.wongOptimal/wongCaution (fill colours), so the same +X% text has different contrast in the two places; the '+N% vs baseline' string is also built twice (deltaLabel and inline in statsCell).

units.does: Renders VStack of the metric chip picker above a ChartCard titled with the selected metric's localized name wrapping metricChartContent.
Shows EmptyState ('No overnight readings in this window') when derived.points is empty, else chartContent(points:).

branches.effect: true: EmptyState explaining naps/spot-checks don't feed Trends; false: chartContent(points:)

units.does: Horizontal non-clipping ScrollView of metric chips, accessibility container labelled 'Metric'.
HStack with one metricChip per Metric.allCases (7 chips).
Builds a capsule Button for a metric; tapping sets selectedMetric (which triggers rebuildDerived via onChange). Selected chip gets tinted fill, primary stroke/foreground and isSelected trait.

branches.effect: true: primary 18% fill; false: cardBackground fill
true: primary 1.2pt stroke; false: clear stroke

units.does: Stacks metricChart with the 'Building baseline' overlay when the 60-day band has <4 samples, then below it shows a scrub pill for the visible point nearest scrubbedDate if the user is dragging.

branches.cond: !band.hasData (fewer than 4 reliable overnight readings in last 60 days for this metric)
branches.effect: true: buildingBaselineOverlay drawn over the chart; false: chart only

branches.cond: scrubbedDate non-nil and a nearest visible point exists
branches.effect: true: scrubPill under the chart; false: nothing

units.does: Returns the newest 120 points (suffix(120)) — the cap the chart, baseline line, scrubbing and audio graph share.

flags.text: The chart silently drops all but the newest 120 readings (e.g. on 'All' with >120 overnights) while the overall card, stats grid and insights use every reading; ARCHITECTURE.md's Trend cap contract says no code path may reduce the set below the selected period and FLOWCHART says 'Nothing else reduces the set'.

units.does: Builds the Swift Chart for the visible (<=120) points: 60-day ±1 SD band + mean rule, daily dots tinted when outside the band, 7-reading rolling line, scrub crosshair; binds chartXSelection to scrubbedDate and attaches an AudioGraph accessibility descriptor.
units.entry: SwiftUI view composition; chartXSelection writes scrubbedDate on drag

branches.effect: true: bandLow = mean - sd; false: nil (no dot tinting)
true: bandHigh = mean + sd; false: nil

units.does: Emits a RectangleMark spanning the visible points' first..last date between mean-sd and mean+sd plus a dashed RuleMark at the mean, only when the band has >=4 samples.

branches.effect: true: band + mean rule; false: no marks
fallback Date() as xStart (only when no points; unreachable here because chart is only built for non-empty points)
fallback Date() as xEnd (same as above)

flags.text: With exactly one visible point (e.g. 7-day range with one overnight while the 60-day baseline has >=4) xStart == xEnd, so the RectangleMark band has zero width and is invisible; only the dashed mean RuleMark shows.

units.does: One PointMark per point (size 30); colour wongCaution when the value is below bandLow or above bandHigh, otherwise primary 70%.

branches.cond: bandLow/bandHigh nil (?? false) or value outside them
branches.effect: outside band: wongCaution dot; inside or no band: primary 0.7 dot

flags.text: Dots outside the 60-day mean ±1 SD are painted wongCaution whichever side they fall on, so a night ABOVE the band on a higher-is-better metric (Recovery, RMSSD, SDNN, HF Power) is shown in the caution colour, while the scrub pill for the same dot colours its delta wongOptimalText (good). The band is a raw arithmetic mean ±1 SD (population), so ~1/3 of normally distributed nights are tinted caution, and for log-normal RMSSD/SDNN/HF it is the raw mean±SD treatment the #19 comment says mis-flags readings.

units.does: Draws the memoized rolling-mean line (derived.rollingBaseline) restricted to points dated at or after the first visible point.

branches.effect: ?? .distantPast: no date restriction (only when visible points empty)

units.does: When scrubbing, draws a dashed vertical RuleMark and an enlarged PointMark at the point nearest scrubbedDate.

branches.effect: true: crosshair + emphasised dot; false: nothing

units.does: Capsule pill with the point's abbreviated month/day, formatted metric value, and '+N% vs baseline' coloured by deltaColor when the 60-day baseline exists and mean > 0.

branches.effect: true: delta text; false: no delta

units.does: 'Building baseline' card (ultra-thin adaptive material, opaque under Reduce Transparency) explaining the band appears after 4 overnight readings in 60 days.

flags.text: Overlay text says the band appears 'once there are 4 overnight readings in the last 60 days', but hasData counts values of the SELECTED metric; Balance/HF Power/Stress skip sessions without frequencyDomain/ansMetrics, so the overlay can stay up with many overnight readings.

units.does: Returns the point whose date is closest (absolute interval) to the given date; nil when pts is empty.
Formats a value for the selected metric: rounded Int with unit (' ms', ' bpm', ' / 100', none for stress), Balance as %.2f in app locale, HF Power rounded with ' ms²'.

branches.effect: true (stress): bare integer; false: integer + space + unit

units.does: Returns localized '<sign><rounded pct>% vs baseline'.

branches.effect: true: '+' prefix; false: '' (minus comes from Int)

units.does: Scrub-pill delta colour: textSecondary when |pct|<5 or metric is Balance; otherwise wongOptimalText if the change is in the good direction (lower for Stress/Mean HR, higher otherwise) else wongCautionText.

branches.effect: true: neutral textSecondary, return; false: continue
true: good = pct < 0; false: good = pct > 0

units.does: Returns whether value lies outside mean ± sd.

flags.text: MetricPoint.outOfBand(mean:sd:) has no caller anywhere in the repo (grep 'outOfBand(mean' / '.outOfBand(' finds only the declaration, tests included); dailyDots recomputes the same test inline.

units.does: Maps sessions to MetricPoints (id/date = startDate) for a metric, dropping sessions without that metric value.
Extracts the metric from a session: recoveryScore×10 (0–10 → 0–100), rmssd/sdnn/meanHR from timeDomain, LF/HF and HF from frequencyDomain, Baevsky stressIndex from ansMetrics; nil when missing.
Trailing simple moving average over `window` consecutive points (not calendar days); returns [] when fewer points than window.

branches.effect: append mean of the window ending there, dated at that point

flags.text: Chart doc calls the line a '7-day rolling baseline' but it averages the last 7 readings regardless of date gaps, so with missed nights it spans weeks.

units.does: Two-column LazyVGrid of derived.stats cells.
Card for one GridCell: uppercase label, large mean value, delta line, subline.
Shows the cell's formatted delta coloured by deltaColor(pct:higherIsBetter:) when present.

branches.effect: true: coloured delta text; false: nothing

units.does: Stats-grid delta colour: textSecondary when direction or pct is nil or |pct|<5; else wongOptimal for the good direction, wongCaution otherwise.

branches.effect: true: good = pct>0; false: good = pct<0

flags.text: Stats-grid delta TEXT is coloured with AppTheme.wongOptimal/wongCaution, which Theme.swift documents as failing WCAG contrast as text on the light theme (wongCaution 2.3:1) and provides wongOptimalText/wongCautionText for; the scrub pill's deltaColor uses the text variants.

units.does: Builds the 4 stats cells (Recovery avg, RMSSD avg, Heart Complexity DFA α1, Stress avg) for the scoped sessions; [] when there are none.
Recovery avg cell from recoveryScore×10, subline '<n> of <N> overnights', delta vs 60-day recovery baseline, higher is better.
RMSSD avg cell (' ms') from analysisResult.timeDomain.rmssd, delta vs 60-day RMSSD baseline (arithmetic mean), higher is better.
Heart Complexity cell: mean DFA α1 formatted %.2f, subline 'DFA α1', no baseline/delta.
Stress avg cell from Baevsky stressIndex, delta vs 60-day stress baseline, higher is worse.
Generic cell builder: arithmetic mean of values formatted, subline '<count> <suffix>', delta % vs baseline mean when baseline has data and |pct| >= 1; '—' and '0 <suffix>' when no values.

branches.effect: deltaPct nil → no delta line; else pct

units.does: Insights heading + card.
Card listing derived.insights as bullet rows (ForEach id \.self).
Wraps one insight in InsightBulletRow at dt14.

Builds insight sentences: <3 points → one 'need at least 3 readings' line; else a direction sentence from TrendVerdict on the metric's scale, a variation (CV) sentence when CV > 0, and an outlier-count sentence when outliers > 0.

branches.effect: return single 'Trends need at least 3 readings' sentence

flags.text: Parameter totalDays (passed scoped.count at TrendsV2View.swift:286) is never used in the body.
buildInsights/variationStats/rawVariationStats have no unit test (grep EmuquTests finds none); only computeDirection is exercised by TrendVerdictTests.

units.does: Maps (direction glyph, optional days) to a whole localized sentence: rising/falling/stable over the last N days or across all readings; any other glyph → 'not enough readings yet'.

branches.effect: 'not enough readings yet to call a trend'

flags.text: Direction is recovered by string-matching SF Symbol names produced by computeDirection; changing a glyph silently turns every sentence into 'not enough readings yet'.

units.does: For RMSSD/SDNN computes CV and outliers in log space (CV = sqrt(exp(sd²)-1)·100, outlier = |ln v - mean| > 2 SD, sample SD); other metrics use rawVariationStats.

flags.text: Only RMSSD/SDNN take the log-space path; HF Power and LF/HF Balance, which trendScale itself treats as logarithmic, go through rawVariationStats whose outlier rule is |v-mean| > 25% of mean — the exact problem the #19 comment describes (normal skewed readings reported as 'well outside your typical range').

units.does: Population CV (%) and count of points more than 25% away from the arithmetic mean.

flags.text: Outlier threshold is a fixed 25% of the mean, not a spread-based band; e.g. for Stress index or Recovery the count does not reflect the user's own variability, yet is presented as 'well outside your typical range'.

units.does: True for .rmssd and .sdnn.
Trend verdict scale per metric: logarithmic for rmssd/sdnn/hfPower/balance, linear for recovery/meanHR/stress.
Labels CV low/normal/high with thresholds 15/30% for log-normal metrics, 8/15% otherwise, and returns 'Day-to-day variation is N% — label.'
Section heading Text at dt13 semibold with detailSectionHeadingStyle.
